animals.text: Some of horror's quietest cruelty falls on the creatures that cannot speak for themselves: the family dog, the kennelled pack, the horses that trust their keepers. At an Antarctic research station, a rescued sled dog [transforms in the kennel and absorbs the other dogs|1982-the-thing]. In Adelaide, a reassembled pop-up book shows [Amelia killing the dog, then her son and herself|2014-the-babadook], and on a California ranch the Haywood siblings watch [their horses panic and vanish into a cloud that never moves|2022-nope]. The fear is rare in the record, and almost all of it is North American.

expectant parents.text: Horror finds a particular dread in the waiting months, when a body carries someone not yet born and every threat counts twice. On a Swedish island, [Alma, pregnant, sits up through the night|1968-hour-of-the-wolf] while her husband sketches the visions that torment him. In Bali a cursed anthropologist's [head tears free and flies off to devour an unborn baby|1981-mystics-in-bali], and in Francoist Spain [Ofelia travels with her pregnant, ailing mother|2006-pan-s-labyrinth] to the house of a captain who tortures and kills. The fear appears nowhere in the record before 1960.

families and parents.text: The oldest horror is the one that comes home, to the people we cannot choose and cannot leave. On a New England farm at the forest's edge, [baby Samuel vanishes in his sister Thomasin's care|2015-the-witch], and grief turns the family against her. In Seoul, [Hyun-seo phones her father Gang-du from the sewers|2006-the-host] where the monster keeps its prey, and in Utah [Annie Graham watches mourning turn to blame between her and her son Peter|2018-hereditary]. Fewer than a quarter of the record's films before 1960 put a family in danger; since 2015 it is half.

friends and companions.text: Friendship is a promise to stay, and horror tests it in places where staying costs everything. A year after losing her husband and daughter, Sarah [joins five friends in a cave that turns out to be unmapped|2005-the-descent], where pale blind creatures hunt by sound. In Chanderi, the ladies' tailor Vicky [loses his friend Jana to a spirit that leaves only clothes behind|2018-stree], and [Maya and her best friend Dini travel to a remote village|2019-impetigore] where children are buried every day. The fear is most common in the record's films from 2000 to 2014.

heirs of old wrongs.text: Some debts outlive the people who ran them up, and the children pay. In 1630s Moldavia the witch Asa curses her brother's line, and two centuries later [she wakes hungry for the life of the melancholy Katia|1960-black-sunday]. Twenty years after a Thakur's crime, [his grandson Kumar hears a woman singing from the swamp|1962-bees-saal-baad], near the tree where his father and grandfather were killed. In Antonio Bay, a century after the founders wrecked a ship for its gold, [the drowned crew roll in with the fog|1980-the-fog] on the eve of the centennial.

meddlers and creators.text: There is a particular horror in being undone by your own hands, by the thing you built, summoned or dug out of the ground. Dr. Weir, who designed the lost ship, [joins the rescue crew aboard the Event Horizon|1997-event-horizon] and finds that each of them begins to see the people they failed. In the rain-cursed village of Tumbbad, Vinayak [lowers himself on a rope to steal gold from the starving god Hastar|2018-tumbbad], with a dough doll for bait. The fear was strongest in the record's earliest decades, the age of Frankenstein (1931) and The Mummy (1932).

monsters who suffer.text: Sometimes the creature is the one in pain, and the film asks us to feel for it. On Dr. Moreau's island, [Lota, a gentle young woman, has fingernails turning back into claws|1932-island-of-lost-souls] while the beast-men scatter at the crack of his whip. In New York, [Irena fears that passion will turn her into a panther|1942-cat-people] and never consummates her marriage. In Louisiana, the young plantation owner Louis [regrets becoming a vampire at once|1994-interview-with-the-vampire] and lives on animal blood rather than kill, while Lestat revels in the hunt.

newcomers and travellers.text: Arriving somewhere new leaves a person without maps, allies or any sense of which doors to avoid. Marion Crane, driving with stolen money, [stops for the night at the secluded Bates Motel|1960-psycho], and the ballet student Suzy Bannion [reaches a Freiburg academy just as another girl flees it in terror|1977-suspiria]. At a lakefront holiday home in Austria, [a polite young man comes to the kitchen to borrow eggs|1997-funny-games], and by nightfall the family are his hostages. The fear peaks in the record's films of the 1960s and 70s.

objects of desire.text: To be wanted can be its own danger, when someone's longing hardens into ownership. In a Mexican circus, the grown Fénix [lends his arms to Concha as her hands|1989-santa-sangre], and offstage she orders him to kill every woman he desires. Across an emptied England, Jim, Selena and Hannah [follow a radio promise of salvation to a soldiers' blockade near Manchester|2002-28-days-later]. Older films carry the fear too, from The Mummy (1932) and Peeping Tom (1960) to Tenebrae (1982), and the record finds it least often in films made since 2015.

outcasts and the marginalised.text: The people horror finds easiest to hurt are those the world has already pushed aside. In Tualang Tiga, [the hunchback Si Bongkok paints beautifully but is shunned for his face|1958-sumpah-orang-minyak], until a devil's bargain makes him the oily man. In Los Angeles, Sarah Bailey [falls in with three outcast girls rumoured to be witches|1996-the-craft], and in Derry [a band of bullied misfits follow the sewer maps|2017-it] because no adult sees what they see. The fear is most common in the record's newest films, a third of them made since 2015.

people at work.text: Work puts people where they would never choose to be: on the night shift, at the edge of the map, alone with someone else's children. Miss Giddens takes her first post as governess at Bly and [begins to see the dead valet Quint in the grounds|1961-the-innocents]. At an Antarctic research station, [MacReady takes command once the radio is smashed|1982-the-thing], trusting no one, and in Paris [Maureen buys clothes for a supermodel while waiting for a sign from her dead twin|2016-personal-shopper]. Roughly a quarter of the record's films put someone in danger because of the job they do.

spouses and lovers.text: Love opens a door that horror walks straight through. In Wisborg, [Ellen reads that only a pure-hearted woman's blood, freely given, can hold Count Orlok|1922-nosferatu], who admired her portrait from his Carpathian castle. The potter Genjūrō sends his wife Miyagi back to shore and [is drawn into marriage by the noblewoman Lady Wakasa|1953-ugetsu], and in upstate New York Chris [spends a weekend with his girlfriend Rose's family|2017-get-out], whose warmth never quite rings true. Before 1960 two in three films in the record put a spouse or lover in danger; later the share falls to between a quarter and a third.

teenagers and young adults.text: Youth is the age of first freedoms, and horror waits at every one of them: the picnic, the party, the night of babysitting. On Valentine's Day 1900, [Miranda, Marion and Irma climb Hanging Rock|1975-picnic-at-hanging-rock] and walk in a trance into a crevice in the stone. In Haddonfield, [Michael Myers shadows the babysitter Laurie Strode|1978-halloween] while her friends laugh off her fears, and in Adelaide [seventeen-year-old Mia joins a party game built around an embalmed severed hand|2022-talk-to-me]. Close to one film in five in the record turns on the danger of being young.

the abused and bullied.text: Some people meet the horror already hurt, by those who should have kept them safe. In a Stockholm suburb, [twelve-year-old Oskar spends his evenings imagining revenge|2008-let-the-right-one-in] on the boys who torment him, until Eli moves in next door and taps messages through the wall. In Tehran, [Shideh and her daughter Dorsa are left alone|2016-under-the-shadow] as missiles fall and the neighbours flee, and at a delta resort in Senegal [a deaf woman named Awa already knows who the mercenaries are|2021-saloum]. Two thirds of the record's films with this fear were made after 2000.

the grieving.text: Grief leaves a door ajar, and the films in this record keep finding what comes through it. John and Laura Baxter [carry their grief for drowned Christine to Venice|1973-don-t-look-now], where John keeps glimpsing a small figure in a red coat. A year after losing her husband and daughter, [Sarah goes down into an unmapped cave|2005-the-descent], and in Adelaide [the widow Amelia still cannot face the crash that killed her husband|2014-the-babadook]. More than half of these films were made since 2015, which makes mourning one of the newest fears in the record.

the guilty punished.text: There is a cold satisfaction in watching wrongdoers pay, and horror rarely lets it stay comfortable. In Kwaidan, [a swordsman who abandoned his devoted wife comes home to a tender welcome|1964-kwaidan] that does not last until morning. Tun and Jane [leave a girl they ran over lying on the road|2004-shutter] and soon see pale faces surface in Tun's photographs, while in Guatemala [the old dictator Enrique Monteverde hears a woman weeping at night|2019-la-llorona] after his genocide verdict is overturned. The fear peaks in the record's films from 2000 to 2014.

the lonely and isolated.text: Loneliness makes a person easy to reach, and the haunted places in these films seem to know it. Eleanor Lance, [lonely and guilty after years nursing her invalid mother|1963-the-haunting], comes to Hill House, where doors close on their own and something pounds at the bedroom door. In Black Sabbath [a call girl alone in her basement flat|1963-black-sabbath] answers threatening calls, and in a decaying Hong Kong tower block [the abandoned actor Chin Siu-ho hangs himself|2013-rigor-mortis] before a retired hunter cuts him down. Nearly half these films come from the years since 2015.

the old, sick and dying.text: Age and illness take away the strength to run, and horror lingers at the bedside. In Paris, [Maureen waits for a sign from her twin brother|2016-personal-shopper], as they promised each other before his heart gave out, and spends a night in his empty house among running taps and a spirit that vomits ectoplasm. The record finds this fear across almost a century, in films as far apart as Vampyr (1932), Cronos (1993), Saint Maud (2019) and The Substance (2024).

the trapped and the surviving.text: Captivity strips a person down to the bare question of whether they will outlast the night. In a Pennsylvania farmhouse, [Ben boards up the windows against a growing horde|1968-night-of-the-living-dead] while a family hides in the cellar. Two strangers [wake chained by the ankle at opposite ends of a derelict bathroom|2004-saw], and Brent [wakes bound to a chair in a house decorated like a dance hall|2009-the-loved-ones], where Lola means to keep her date for good. More than four in ten of these films were made since 2015.

those consumed from within.text: The most intimate horror happens inside a person, as a mind turns on itself or something else moves in. In an abandoned palace in Allahabad, [a woman's singing draws Hari Shankar through the empty rooms|1949-mahal]. In a small Brazilian town, [the undertaker Zé do Caixão scorns religion|1964-at-midnight-i-ll-take-your-soul] and kills his wife and his friend, and in Bali [Cathy Kean's head tears free and flies off|1981-mystics-in-bali] after the Queen of the Leák carves a spell into her thigh. The fear was strongest before 1960, the era of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1931) and The Wolf Man (1941).

those who step in.text: Someone always has to knock on the door, open the case or say the prayer, and they rarely walk away untouched. In Georgetown, [Father Damien Karras, a priest losing his faith|1973-the-exorcist], is called to a girl on whose stomach the words 'help me' rise. The journalist [Reiko Asakawa traces a cursed videotape to a cabin in Izu|1998-ringu] and starts her own seven days, and [five police officers answer a late call for backup|2015-baskin] that ends at an abandoned Ottoman-era police station. More than one film in five in the record carries this fear, most often from the 1980s on.

whole communities.text: Some horrors are too large for one house and settle over a whole town. In Wisborg, [the streets fill with deaths blamed on a plague from Orlok's ship|1922-nosferatu]. In Kurouzu-cho, [the whole town is caught in the spiral|2000-uzumaki] as classmates sprout shells and climb the school walls, and in the mountains of South Korea [a bizarre infection drives the villagers of Gokseong to kill their own families|2016-the-wailing]. The fear was commonest in the record's earliest films, touching a third of those made before 1960.

young children.text: The smallest people are the ones horror most often reaches for, because they cannot protect themselves and their parents cannot always do it for them. At Bly, the governess [watches over the orphans Flora and Miles|1961-the-innocents] while figures appear in the grounds. In a closed orphanage, [Simón draws his new friend Tomás in a sack mask|2007-the-orphanage] before he disappears, and in Indonesia a cult's price is the last child, and [six-year-old Ian, who is deaf, turns seven in three days|2017-satan-s-slaves]. Barely one film in fourteen put a child in danger before 1960; since 2015 it is more than one in four.
